chapter: Return to Atlanta and move north
title: Edwina Sutton's Buddy Bradley portrait and two and a half years in Philadelphia
summary: Robey leaves the boys with Edwina Sutton, whose husband admired Buddy Bradley; Green learns who Bradley's students were.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, uh-huh. See now, as we were traveling, you see, and we got -- finally got to Philadelphia, he stopped at a place -- Miss Edwina Sutton's place down in Philadelphia somewhere on -- think it was North Philadelphia where she was. And she had a big picture of Mr. Buddy Bradley, you know, because her husband was in import and export, you see. He traveled on the seas, you see, and he

was a fan of Buddy Bradley's, you know, and he liked Buddy Bradley, and he had this picture; it was like a portrait; it was in the living room, and she liked us. So Mr. Robey had her to -- (inaudible) like as a guardian. She would look after us children while he would -- he'd like go -- he went over to New York with Obi Walker somewhere, you know, and he got him some fights or something, you know.

Then he came back, see. He came back. So we stayed in Philadelphia with this lady for about two and a half years, because we were getting older, see. You had to be 18 years old in order to appear on the stage then. So --
Explain what you were just telling me.

Well now, she was taking care of us, see, and I used to see this portrait of Mr. Buddy Bradley. He was about the greatest tap dance teacher that they had. He had students like Eleanor Powell. Really, first he had Ruby Keeler and some other lady that became famous in the movies. I think her name was Arlene Judge and I think another one that became famous in the movies. Yeah, --
Yeah, Priscilla Lane and some girl named -- what was her name -- Graham, I think, some Gloria Graham.

Yeah, Lucille Ball, Rita Hayworth, people like that. And I used to ask Miss Sutton, ask her about who is that man, you know. And she explained that he was the great -- he was the great tap dancer, you know, in show business, and her husband was a fan of his. They were kind of friends of some sort, you know.
